context: Chord diagram showing bilateral trade flows (exports and imports in $B) between 10 countries: USA, China, Germany, Japan, UK, France, S. Korea, India, Canada, Mexico. Single view with arc-hover isolation and ribbon-hover tooltip interactions.
first_impression: The center ribbon tangle is visually dense and difficult to parse at a glance, though the dominant USA-China-Canada-Mexico flows are immediately legible due to their size.
what_works: The hover-to-isolate interaction is well-designed and directly addresses the core perceptual problem of ribbon overlap — dimming non-relevant chords to near-zero opacity makes individual trade relationships traceable. Arc sizes immediately communicate trade volume rank without any reading.
what_doesnt: With 10 categories, the palette has two near-similar blues (#4477AA vs #88CCEE) and two near-similar greens (#228833 vs #117733) that are hard to distinguish in the dense ribbon interior where colors mix and overlap. At static view the center is a near-hairball — smaller flows like India and France are nearly invisible ribbons buried under the dominant USA/China/Canada/Mexico chords, and the label for S. Korea is clipped to 'i. Korea' due to rotation/truncation.
